'''Rafael Paulo de Lara Araújo'''<ref name=fsp/> ({{IPA|pt-BR|ʁafaˈɛw aɾaˈuʒu|lang}}; born August 12, 1980) is a Brazilian former professional [[basketball]] player. He played for three years in the [[National Basketball Association]].

==College career==
After attending Padre Anacleto High School in [[São Paulo]], Araújo went to the [[United States]] to play [[college basketball]], attending [[Arizona Western College]] in [[Yuma, Arizona]]. In his freshman season (2000–01), he averaged 12.1 points and 8.4 rebounds per game.<ref name=draft2004profile>[http://www.nba.com/draft2004/profiles/RafaelAraujo.html Prospect Profile: Rafael Araujo (Ha-fay-el Ar-RU-joe)]</ref> Araújo later explained that AWC coach Kelly Green gave him $400 to get his [[Visa (document)|visa]] and establish himself in Yuma, despite coaches being forbidden to do so.<ref name=fsp/> As a sophomore, he tallied 17.9 points and 10.7 rebounds per game,<ref name=draft2004profile/> leading the Matadors to a 28–3 record and a top ten national ranking among junior colleges.<ref name=draft2004profile/> He was named Region Most Valuable Player and 2nd Team [[NJCAA]] All-American.<ref name=draft2004profile/> At the same time Araújo  was drafted for the [[Brazil national basketball team]] at the [[2002 FIBA World Championship|2002 World Championships]], as NBA player [[Nenê]] could not attend the tournament.<ref name=fsp/>

After finishing his junior college career, Araújo moved to [[Brigham Young University]] in [[Provo, Utah]] where as a junior (2002–03), he averaged 12.0 points and 8.9 rebounds per game<ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/team/stats/_/id/252/byu-cougars Brigham Young Cougars Statistics - 2002-03]</ref> (second in the [[Mountain West Conference]]). In his senior season, Araújo led BYU in scoring (18.4 points per game), rebounding (10.1 rebounds per game), steals (43 total), and blocked shots (25).<ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/team/stats/_/id/252/byu-cougars Brigham Young Cougars Statistics - 2003-04]</ref> He was named Co-Player of the Year in the Mountain West Conference, sharing the honor with [[United States Air Force|Air Force]]'s Nick Welch.<ref name=reprimanded>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=1755344 Araujo still eligible for MWC tourney]</ref><ref name=punch/> He was named 2nd Team NCAA [[All-American]] by ''Basketball Times'' and Honorable Mention All-American by the [[Associated Press]].

With his size and strength, the 6-foot-11, 295-pound Araújo impressed many pro scouts during his senior season. On December 6, 2003, he dominated a tough [[Oklahoma State University - Stillwater|Oklahoma State]] team, totaling 32 points and 17 rebounds in BYU's 76–71 upset victory.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20040111042013/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=233400252 BYU 76, Oklahoma State 71]</ref>  He concluded his collegiate career with a 24-point, 12-rebound performance in the Cougars' 80–75 loss to [[Syracuse University|Syracuse]] in the NCAA Tournament.<ref name=draft2004profile/><ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20040411191346/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=244000035 McNamara drains nine 3s for career-high 43]</ref>

==Controversy==
During the 2002 World Championships in [[Indianapolis, Indiana|Indianapolis]], Araújo tested positive for the steroid [[nandrolone]]. He was given a 24-month suspension from international play. He was subsequently found clean during tests while a player at [[Brigham Young University|BYU]], and the NBA did not test players for steroid use.<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120710102846/http://deseretnews.com/dn/view/0,1249,595076947,00.html|title=Deseret Morning News {{!}} Araujo finishing steroid suspension}}</ref> Araújo explained that the tests went positive because at the time he consumed a [[dietary supplement]] containing [[androstenedione]], but he could still play because he was only suspended by [[FIBA]], who does not sanction college basketball.<ref name=fsp/>

Araújo was involved in multiple on-court incidents during his senior season at BYU.  On March 6, 2004, Araújo was reprimanded by the Mountain West Conference (MWC) for hitting UNLV guard [[Jerel Blassingame]] during an 89–88 win.<ref name=reprimanded/><ref name=punch>[https://web.archive.org/web/20080214083015/http://www.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/stories/031004aaq.html Mountain West Conference Reprimands Araujo], March 9, 2004</ref> Six days later on March 12, in a 54–51 loss to [[University of Utah|Utah]], Araujo was charged with a technical foul for elbowing the [[Utah Utes|Utes]]' [[Andrew Bogut]] in the head in the MWC Tournament.<ref>[http://www.byucougars.com/Filing.jsp?ID=4983 GAME 29 RECAP -- HEARTBREAKER ENDS COUGARS VICTORY STREAK]</ref>

==Professional career==
The [[Toronto Raptors]] selected Araújo with the eighth pick in the [[2004 NBA draft]], making him the first college senior drafted that year, one pick ahead of future NBA finals MVP Andre Iguodala. His NBA career was mostly disappointing with him seeing limited action as a rookie, averaging 3.3 points and 3.1 rebounds in 12.5 minutes per game.<ref>[http://www.cbssports.com/nba/players/playerpage/498271 Rafael Araújo Player Page]</ref> He set a career-high with 14 rebounds against the [[Sacramento Kings]] on January 5, 2005. Days later, on January 9, he scored a career-high 14 points against the [[Golden State Warriors]]. He later matched that total against the Kings on November 25, 2005.

In the [[2005-06 NBA season|2005-06 season]], he again struggled through a disappointing year and had trouble getting playing time, averaging 11.6 minutes a game, 2.3 points, and 2.8 rebounds while shooting a dismal 36.6% from the field. Shortly after that season, Toronto GM [[Rob Babcock]] was fired, and it was rumored that the firing, in part, had to do with the drafting of Araújo.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2475953 Raptors Trade Bust Araújo to Jazz]</ref> The player claimed he did not play much with the Raptors because then-coach [[Sam Mitchell (basketball)|Sam Mitchell]] held a grudge against Babcock, and thus he did not want to put Babcock's draft pick on the court.<ref name=fsp/>

On June 8, 2006, Araújo was traded to the [[Utah Jazz]] with an undisclosed amount of money for [[Kris Humphries]] and [[Robert Whaley]].  Many viewed this as a new beginning for Araújo, a chance for him to change the direction of his career.  He worked hard in Utah, dropping his weight from 295 pounds to 275 in an effort to improve his athleticism.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20121022233328/http://www.deseretnews.com/article/640193891/Whaley-despite-being-traded-is-back-with-Jazz.html Big Loss for Araújo]</ref> He also expressed much interest as he already played in Utah during college. However, he did not fit in well in Utah's offense, which was already set with [[Carlos Boozer]], [[Andrei Kirilenko]] and [[Mehmet Okur]] in the frontcourt,<ref name=fsp/> and Araújo played sparingly during the [[2006-07 NBA season|2006-07 season]].  He averaged 2.6 points and 2.4 rebounds per game in 28 games, averaging only 8.9 minutes per appearance.

Araújo's rookie contract expired after the 2006–07 season, and Jazz owner [[Larry H. Miller]] said publicly that he liked Araújo and hoped he could return to the team the following season.<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120729004100/http://www.deseretnews.com/article/680195423/Miller-expects-to-re-sign-Araujo.html|title=Miller Hopes To Re-sign Araujo}}</ref> Araújo's final NBA game was played in Game 5 of the 2007 Western Conference Finals against the [[San Antonio Spurs]] on May 30, 2007. Utah will lose the game 84 - 109, with Araújo recording 7 points, 4 rebounds and 1 steal. San Antonio thus won the entire series 4 - 1.

Araújo played for Utah in the 2007 [[Rocky Mountain Revue]], but the Jazz signed 7-foot-1 [[Kyrylo Fesenko]] during the offseason, filling the roster spot that Araújo held previously.  With that opportunity gone, and his NBA career likely over, Araújo signed a 1-year, $500,000 contract to play for [[Spartak Saint Petersburg|Spartak St. Petersburg]] in Russia.<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120707124054/http://deseretnews.com/dn/view/0,5143,695203799,00.html|title=Araujo finds a home with Russian Team}}</ref> Araújo claimed that despite the easy adaptation, his lack of European passport and Spartak's underperformances led him to leave.<ref name=nbb/>

Araújo was in training camp with the NBA's [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] for 2008 but was waived before the [[2008-09 NBA season|2008-09 season]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/wolves_waive_araujo_081012.html Timberwolves Waive Center Rafael Araujo]</ref> He claimed that this happened because of the arrival of [[Kevin Love]],<ref name=fsp/> and because Araújo was not in top shape due to an injured knee.<ref name=nbb>[http://www.basketbrasil.com.br/2009/06/06/baby-nao-tive-muitas-oportunidades-na-nba-e-as-que-tive-nao-foram-justas/ Baby: “Não tive muitas chances (na NBA) e as que tive não foram justas”] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111130033952/http://www.basketbrasil.com.br/2009/06/06/baby-nao-tive-muitas-oportunidades-na-nba-e-as-que-tive-nao-foram-justas/ |date=2011-11-30 }} {{in lang|pt}}</ref>

After a brief and failed stint at the [[Shanghai Sharks]],<ref name=fsp/> in January 2009, Araújo signed with Brazilian club [[Flamengo Basketball|Flamengo]] for the 2009 season. The details of his contract were not revealed. He became the star of the club's team alongside [[Marcelinho Machado]].<ref>[http://globoesporte.globo.com/Esportes/Noticias/Basquete/0,,MUL945798-15060,00.html Ex-pivô da NBA já treina no Flamengo] {{in lang|pt}}</ref> Six months later, at the end of the 2009 season, he signed a deal with [[Club Athletico Paulistano (basketball)|Paulistano]] for the 2009–10 season, and in June 2010 he transferred back to [[Flamengo Basketball|Flamengo]] signing a two-year contract. For his second stint at Flamengo, Araújo, for [[numerology]] reasons, changed the spelling of his nickname to "Bàbby" and his jersey number from 55 to 66.<ref name=fsp/>

Araújo made headlines in January 2011 by [[backboard shattering|shattering a glass backboard]] with a powerful dunk during a game in the [[FIBA Americas League]].  Video of the play was widely circulated across the Internet.<ref>[http://www.huffingtonpost.com/2011/01/17/rafael-araujo-shatters-backboard_n_809759.html Rafael Araújo Shatters Backboard]</ref>

In June 2011, he signed a deal with [[Franca Basquetebol Clube]]. In 2012, Araújo decided to retire, though he was open to return to basketball if he had a good proposal.<ref name=fsp>{{cite news|url=http://acervo.folha.com.br/fsp/2012/03/25/20/5762271|language=pt|title=Tombo Gigante|newspaper=[[Folha de S. Paulo]]|author=Brito, Daniel|date=2012-03-25|access-date=2012-03-26}}</ref>

In October 2012, Araujo returned to basketball, signing with [[Grêmio Esportivo Mogiano|Mogi das Cruzes]].<ref>[https://www.latinbasket.com/Brazil/basketball.aspx?NewsID=293042 Baby is back after retirement ]</ref> He moved to [[Esporte Clube Pinheiros (basketball)|Pinheiros]] in 2014.
